name: Post-Earnings IV-Crush Short Put
summary: Sell a cash-secured put immediately after an earnings report, capturing elevated residual IV once the binary event risk has already resolved.

legs.strike_rule: Delta -0.20 to -0.30, strike below the post-report low

greeks.vega: negative - and here it works for you, since residual post-report IV usually continues to decay for several sessions

when_to_use: The session after a report, when binary risk is gone but IV has not fully normalised (IVR still above 30 and above the name's 60-day median).
entry_rules: Entry window: the session after the report, through 3 trading days after
IVR still > 30 AND current IV > the name's 60-day median IV
Strike below the post-report intraday low, and delta between -0.20 and -0.30 - take whichever is lower
No further earnings before expiry (verified against the next scheduled report date)
Standard liquidity gates: ADV >= 2M, OI >= 500, spread <= 8% of mid
Do not submit before 10:00 ET - post-report spreads need 30 minutes to normalise
management_rules: Buy to close at 50% of credit or at 21 DTE, whichever first
Roll down and out for a credit if delta exceeds -0.50; maximum 2 rolls
If IV normalises quickly and the position reaches 50% within a week, take it and redeploy - that is the strategy working as designed
exit_rules: Close at 50% of credit, 21 DTE, or the 2.5x stop
All never-assign rules apply: extrinsic < $0.10, delta > -0.85, within 1.0% of the strike at 14:30 ET on expiration day, hard backstop 15:45 ET
assignment_risk: MODERATE. Same profile as a standard CSP; choosing the strike below the post-report low reduces but does not remove it.
liquidity_needs: OI >= 500, spread <= 8% of mid after the first 30 minutes of trading.
common_mistakes: Selling into a name that gapped down and is still falling - the IV is high for a reason; choosing the strike by delta alone and ignoring the post-report low.
